lines: If that is so, you have done what nobody at this post could do. I will not thank you for it, and I will not weep for him.

I am Seven-Floods. The man is Walks-Far. The younger woman, who nurses my cough, is Mends-Nets. The Rose's heirs hold us, and a fire in the Rose, the old prison where they keep their held, is why they brought us north to this post.
Tsaxi counted us each day, and his word was the only count. Now nobody can swear how many we are. Any one of us could walk out of here. So could all three of us. No one is left to say it was wrong.

infos.prompt: Who are you?
lines: I am Third-Born Tsaxi, gate-keeper of the Rose's outer post. The Rose is the old prison, far to the north of here. The heirs hold it now as their home, and they set me to watch these three.

I was born in the Rose, and the heirs fed me and raised me. They keep the gate shut on the dead levels below it, and they set me to watch the three at their post. I have never been further from the Rose than this shore.
I cannot read a leaf or a mark, so I know these three by looking, and I say what I see to the heirs without a mistake.
If my count is wrong, my neck answers for it. Ask what you want to know, and ask it plain. I answer plain.

infos.prompt: Who are the three you keep here?
lines: You come from the north house. I know the Broker's children when I see them, and I say that once and no more. I will not explain it. Ask the woman who sent you.

A fire went through the upper floors of the Rose. The heirs sent three of their held up to me, to keep until the Rose's leaves came after them. The leaves are the pages that say what each person is held for. I cannot read them, so a reckoner was to carry them and read them out. A reckoner is the one who reads the Rose's leaves and keeps its count.

The three are a young man, a young woman and an old woman. The old woman is held for a roof: she owes the heirs for the shelter they gave her. One of the two young ones is held for words said in the yard. The other is held for a killing, and when the leaf is read that one will be put under. To be put under is to be sent down below the Rose, past the gate, where the dead still walk. Nobody comes up.
Which of the two young ones is which, I do not know. Both say they are the one held for words. Both can say the words. I was given them at this post, and I did not count what their hands had done.

Hear what I can do. I can lose one of the three to the smoke, and the heirs will believe it, because people die in fires. I cannot lose two. Two is a hunt, and the hunt ends at my neck. So only one can leave this post, and it is for you to say which.

The reckoner came north by the wet road round the west of the lake. He had four with him, and none came back. His camp is the hut in the swamp, far west of the town, round the lake by the wet road. I do not say what is in that swamp. I say five men went into it and none came back, so go armed or do not go. If you find his leaves, read them before you choose. I cannot, and no one here can.

infos.prompt: How did the dead man die?
lines: His name was Otheel. He was a shelter-reckoner of the Rose, one who reckoned what a household owes the heirs for its roof.
He was drowned in a net in the wash-pool, the pool in the Rose where the held wash. I say how he died. I do not say who did it.
Whoever reads the leaves will know who. I can say who stands before me, and I cannot say what their hands did.
The three are east of me, on the water's edge. Speak to them, and think about what you hear.

infos.prompt: Count one of them lost to the smoke.

Now choose which, and tell the one you choose. The other two stay as the heirs set them, and I will keep them on this shore.
If you have found my reckoner's leaves, read them before you choose. I cannot read them, so I cannot tell you if you are wrong. Do not send out the wrong one because you were in a hurry.

infos.prompt: Count one of them lost to the smoke.

infos.prompt: Who are you?
lines: I am Walks-Far. I am the one the heirs hold for words. They run the Rose, the old prison far to the north of here, and they hold me at this post.
I said it in the Rose's yard, and I say it again. "The gate to the dead levels should be opened, and the Rose left." The dead levels are the floors below the Rose, where the dead still walk.
I said it loud, so everyone would hear. Three seasons. That is what I owe for it, and I will not take back one word.
The woman here says she is the one held for words. She stood in the yard. She can say it as well as I can. Saying a thing is not the same as saying it first.

I heard Tsaxi talk, so I know one of us may go. If you take her, a woman who said nothing walks out under my name. I stay, the gate stays shut, and the next man who says it will know what it earns. Take me. I am sick of this water.

infos.prompt: Who are you?
lines: I am Mends-Nets. I was set to mend the heirs' nets, and at night I sit with the old woman, because she coughs through the night with the smoke in her chest. Forgive me if I speak low. She sleeps badly.
I am the one they hold for words. I said them in the yard, and the words are these. "Open the gate to the dead levels, and leave the Rose."
The whole yard heard it, so I have them by heart. The man here says they are his. I do not argue with him. He is frightened, and a frightened man holds hard to what he has.

Think of what is lost if he goes. He is loud, and he cannot keep still. He will say it again at the first wall he finds, and the heirs will hear him, and the hunt will follow the sound to the old woman's tree. I know how to be quiet. I have been quiet at this post a long time.
If he goes, I stay. I sit with her until she is gone, and then I sit alone. I do not ask for pity. I ask you to think about it.

infos.prompt: Who are you?

I want one thing, to die near my Hist. That is the tree I was hatched under, and a woman who dies in the heirs' hands dies far from it.

My daughter is Rows-For-Another. She works off an Owing of her own on the land north of the town. About that Owing I will tell you this much: the girl who kept the count wept when she wrote my daughter down, and then she wrote it.

As for my reckoner, I have decided he turned off the wet road and went home to the Rose another way. Whatever is said of a camp in the swamp, I choose to believe he lives. I need to believe it, because I have no one else to believe in.
